observedProviderError.message: The compiled grammar is too large, which would cause performance issues. Simplify your tool schemas or reduce the number of strict tools.
observedProviderError.classification: PRE-INFERENCE EXECUTION/INFRASTRUCTURE EVENT — not model behaviour, and not scored as any.

measurement.note: the capability-PRESENT schema is only ~440 bytes larger than the capability-ABSENT one, and one is accepted while the other is rejected. BYTE SIZE IS NOT THE PROVIDER METRIC — grammar complexity is, and an enum-constrained array of strings adds disproportionately to it. The vNext first-pass schema is sitting at the edge of the provider grammar budget and the governed-binding capability does not fit inside what is left.

whatThisDoesNotShow: that the capability contract is WRONG. §198 case C proved it is well formed and §199 case H proved every supplied id is visible. What is shown is that the resulting request is not transportable to THIS provider under strict tool-schema mode.

candidateDirectionsForTheSuccessor.change: materially shorten the vNext schema descriptions — they are the bulk of the grammar
candidateDirectionsForTheSuccessor.effect: buys headroom for the capability without changing any contract
candidateDirectionsForTheSuccessor.cost: the descriptions are load-bearing prompt engineering; §104/§105/§138 each measured behaviour changes from description wording, so shortening them is a TREATMENT change requiring its own validation

candidateDirectionsForTheSuccessor.change: represent governedEvidenceSourceIds as an unconstrained string array rather than an enum, and rely on the boundary alone
candidateDirectionsForTheSuccessor.effect: removes the enum grammar entirely; the projection already refuses an unsupplied id by exact set membership
candidateDirectionsForTheSuccessor.cost: gives up the transport-level closed set — the same trade §198 made for the empty case, now for the nonempty one

candidateDirectionsForTheSuccessor.change: split the first pass into two calls, one of which carries the governed binding
candidateDirectionsForTheSuccessor.effect: each request stays inside the grammar budget
candidateDirectionsForTheSuccessor.cost: doubles first-pass calls and makes the analysis non-atomic

candidateDirectionsForTheSuccessor.change: drop strict tool-schema mode for the first pass
candidateDirectionsForTheSuccessor.cost: loses transport-level validation entirely and would be a large protocol change
